_meta.note: battle-tempo battle-resources (2026-09-05). The share of BaseHp(theta) each of the six actor resource pools gets as its max, per-mille. A PROJECTION of the shipped ladder, never a second curve (spec S2.2): resource.max.{id} = BaseHp(theta) * poolShareMilli[id] / 1000, so the only new numbers in the whole module are the six shares below. hp is absent on purpose -- it mirrors BattleActorSetup.MaxHp directly (spec S2.6) rather than deriving, because two disagreeing HP maxima is worse than an incomplete row.
_meta.rebalance: Never hand-edit this file. python tools/tuning/publish.py battle-resources <dotted.key>=<value> [...] writes battle-resources.v{n+1}.json; the old version stays on disk for revert.
_meta.balanceStatus: UNMEASURED placeholders, shipped per the same posture action-timing.v1.json and reaction-lane.v1.json already used in this program: 'shipping a guess is fine, calling it balance is not'. The shares are DELIBERATELY UNIFORM -- no measurement exists that would justify making poise scarcer than qi, and inventing a differentiation we cannot defend would be worse than an honest flat placeholder. Per-id rows exist so a balance pass can differentiate later as a config edit, never a schema change.
_meta.sizing: 500 per-mille against the shipped pin (BaseHp(20) = 680, power-scale.v2.json curve.pinValue) gives a pool of 340 at theta=20. reaction-lane.v1.json's poiseSpend is 100, so a pinned actor affords ~3 counters in a battle. That is the only sanity anchor behind this number -- it is a starting point for RL3's sizing pass, not a balance decision.
_meta.regenIsAbsentOnPurpose: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-14 (lawn-combat-wire T11, spec-lawn-combat-calibration.md). This used to say there was no regen block at all -- ResourceChannelReader.RegenPerTick rounded the channel to a whole long, so the smallest expressible non-zero rate accrued ~300 poise per round against a spend of 100 (three counters a round, erasing the scarcity poise exists to create), and there was nothing representable between that and zero. resource-subtick (S10.1, 2026-09-13) resolved the REPRESENTATION problem: the reader now carries a per-mille-per-tick remainder instead of rounding, so 999 rates exist between nothing and a whole unit. This file now authors exactly ONE non-zero regen row -- stamina, for the lawn/battle basic attack -- and leaves the other four at 0 deliberately, not by omission: poise's original scarcity argument still holds verbatim (nothing changed its spend economics, resource-hub-ssot.md SS11 pools 'refill AT REST' and a battle/lawn encounter is not a rest), and hunger/spirit/qi have no cost mechanism spending them yet, so authoring a rate for them would be inventing a balance number nothing consumes. See _meta.regenDerivation for the stamina arithmetic.
_meta.regenDerivation: RETUNED 2026-10-05 (sustainable-fire band, owner decision): derived at the BAND FLOOR theta=1, not only at the pin. poolMax(theta) = BaseHp(theta) * poolShareMilli.stamina / 1000 and regenPerSecond(theta) = poolMax * regenPerSecondShareMilli.stamina / 1000, so both grow with the power ladder, while action-corpus-cost-templates kinds.basic.baseAmountAtRung1 is a FLAT 25 with no theta term. The sustainable ceiling (regenPerSecond * 1.5s, a Peashooter attack interval measured live 2026-09-13) therefore has to clear 25 at the SMALLEST reachable theta, and the smallest reachable theta is 1, not the pin. At theta=1: BaseHp(1) = 106 on the shipped power-scale.v2.json ladder, poolMax = 106 * 500 / 1000 = 53. 25 <= regenPerSecond * 1.5 needs regenPerSecond >= 16.667, so the smallest whole rate is 17, and 53 * R / 1000 >= 17 needs R >= 321. regenPerSecondShareMilli.stamina is therefore 321 (was 50): the SMALLEST publishable share that holds the whole reachable band theta=1..5000. 320 is one step short and is the proof the minimum is real: 53 * 320 / 1000 = 16, ceiling 24.0, which is under the cost of 25. poolShareMilli is deliberately UNCHANGED at 500 for every resource. Pool and regen scale together, so raising the pool would buy the same regen at the price of doubling burst depth (a full pool affords 2 swings at theta=1 before this publish and still affords 2 after it), and the pool size is separately load-bearing for burst depth and for the reaction-lane poiseSpend 100 anchor at the pin; only the regen lever was needed. Measured through BattleRuleset.BaseHp / BattleResourceMax / BattleResourceRegen with poolShareMilli.stamina=500 and this share: theta=1 poolMax 53, regen 17/s, ceiling 25.50, duty 100 percent (was regen 2/s, ceiling 3.00, duty 12 percent); theta=10 poolMax 180, regen 57/s, ceiling 85.50; theta=19 poolMax 323, regen 103/s, ceiling 154.50; theta=20 poolMax 340, regen 109/s, ceiling 163.50, 6.54x the flat cost (was 17/s, 25.50, 1.02x); theta=30 poolMax 520, regen 166/s, ceiling 249.00, 9.96x; theta=100 poolMax 2340, regen 751/s, ceiling 1126.50, 45.06x. poolMax(20) is still 340, so _meta.sizing and the about-three-counters-at-the-pin anchor are unaffected by this publish. The margin RATIO still grows with theta, because that divergence is the ladder itself and no share value removes it: this publish guarantees the floor, it does not flatten the ceiling. The other four ids stay an explicit 0 for the reasons in _meta.regenIsAbsentOnPurpose, which this retune does not touch: nothing about their spend economics moved.
